blocks.text: AI Posture policies are queries or rules that AI Security define to protect your cloud resources from potential threats and improve your cloud security posture. Policies provide guidelines for managing and protecting your organization's sensitive data and ensuring it is stored securely and only shared with authorized users.

AI Security scans the resources against the policies enabled in your Amazon Web Services (AWS) accounts, Azure subscriptions, and Google Cloud Storage; identifies where the sensitive data is located, vulnerabilities such as any misconfigurations, presence of malware, or if the resource is publicly exposed to the internet; and potential breach possibilities. AI Security generates issues that help you prioritize an incident and quickly remediate the issue. The policies are grouped by threat categories.

AI Security offers predefined policies that are aligned with industry standard cybersecurity and compliance benchmarks such as NIST, GDPR, PCI, etc. You can create custom policies to meet your organization's requirements. AI Security also provides predefined policies that use advanced options to scan the data.
AI Posture policies provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: View all the policies offered by AI Security.
Gain AI posture overview based on whether the policies are passing or failing for your resources.
Create custom security policies to meet your organization's compliance requirements.
Enable or disable policies on resources.

blocks.text: On the Policy page (Policies & Controls > AI Posture Policies), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Apply filters to view specific data.
Add additional filters.
Search for a specific policy.
Add a custom policy.
View the policy details. For each policy, you can view:
Policy Name: The policy title.
Severity: The severity level (Critical, High, Medium, or Low) of the policy.
Policy Source: Whether the policy is a predefined or a custom policy.
Primary Resource Type: The type of resource on which the policy is applied.
Last Updated: The date and time the policy was last updated.
Cloud: The cloud type in which the resource is located.
ID: The unique identifier for the policy.
Created: The date and time the policy was created.
Policy Category: The category (Public Exposure, Data Loss, etc.) to which this policy belongs.
Policy Status: The status (Enabled or Disabled) of the policy.
Select multiple policies to either enable or disable them.
See image.
Click the policy name to view additional details. To learn more, see Viewing Policy Details.
Sort the column data.
View the list of policy categories associated with the policy.
Enable or disable the policy.
Select any of the following actions:
Enable: Enable a policy. This option is available only when the policy is disabled.
Disable: Disable a policy. This option is available only when the policy is enabled.
Clone: Clone a policy.
Change Severity: Change the severity level of the policy. This option is available only when the policy is disabled.
Edit: Edit a custom policy. This option is available only when the policy is disabled.
Delete: Delete a custom policy. This option is available only when the policy is disabled.
You cannot edit, delete, or change the severity level for predefined policies.
Show or hide the columns.
